title: Throughput Sentry: Margin-Regulated Scaling Engine for Dedicated Fleets
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Goal: implement a robust autoscaling engine for Dedicated fleets that targets a composite throughput-margin metric and enforces conservative safety limits to guarantee tenant throughput SLAs while minimizing cost and noisy oscillation.

Background: current autoscalers either chase raw p95/p99 latency signals (risk: overreact to short tails) or use simple throughput thresholds (risk: sustained underprovisioning for bursty traffic). We need a hybrid approach for Dedicated that: 1) targets effective tenant throughput (tokens/s or requests/s normalized to model type), 2) maintains a configurable margin (headroom) to absorb burst variance, and 3) applies deterministic step/rate limits and rollback policies to avoid cascading scale events across the fleet.

Scope: design and implement the \"Throughput Sentry\" policy module in the autoscaler service: target metric definition, forecasting component (lightweight Holt-Winters rolling window), scaling algorithm (bounded additive + revertible reservoir), and safety envelope rules (max-step, cooldown, tenant-caps, cross-tenant backoff). Integration points include: capacity planner, router fallback, console exposure for per-route targets, and telemetry for post-rollout evaluation.

Non-goals: full ML-based long horizon forecasting, per-tenant economic optimization (will be a follow-up), hardware auto-placement optimizer.

Key design decisions: 1) Composite target metric = EWMA(normalized_throughput) + latency_penalty_score. Normalization maps model type and sequence-length distribution to baseline tokens/sec per GPU. 2) Forecasting horizon limited to 60s using Holt-Winters variant to prioritize recency and low compute. 3) Scaling increments use an additive step proportional to forecasted shortfall but clipped by max_step_percent (default 20% of current pool). 4) Enforce cooldown window (default 2 minutes) and progressive rollback (if scaled up then error rate rises, rollback to previous capacity and mark route for manual review). 5) Tenant isolation: per-tenant burst credit bucket with refill rate tied to committed throughput quota. 6) Safe-fail behavior: when telemetry is missing or noisy, fallback to conservative static headroom profile rather than aggressive scaling.

Trade-offs and rationale: we favor predictability and safety over aggressive cost savings for Dedicated customers with throughput guarantees. Using a short-horizon forecast reduces oscillation compared to instant reactive controllers, at the cost of occasional underprovision during sudden spikes. The additive clipped step prevents exponential growth that can exhaust shared infra. Latency is treated as a penalty rather than primary target to avoid noisy latency spikes from influencing capacity for low-volume tenants.

Implementation notes: autoscaler will expose policy parameters via the console and allow per-tenant overrides. Default params optimized from benchmark runs in internal cluster \"dedicated-load-03\" with model family Llama-2-70B and sequence lengths sampled from production traces. The code changes will land under repo: github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler (module autoscaler/policies/throughput_sentry). A feature flag (throughput_sentry_v1) will gate rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Autoscaler supports composite metric (normalized_throughput + latency_penalty) and calculates short-horizon forecasts
Scaling decisions respect max_step_percent and cooldown windows and do not cause >2x capacity jumps in a single event
Per-tenant burst credit mechanism implemented and configurable via tenant config API
Fallback behavior when telemetry missing: uses conservative static headroom profile
End-to-end bench: sustained 30% traffic surge for 90s results in <100ms p95 tail regressions and no SLO violations for committed tenants
Policy params surfaced in Console UI and persisted through tenant config API
